done: BASE: master 85c3dda, in worktree concordance-2-canons on branch full-canons. One step, canons. It ships with sh tools/deploy.sh after green CI, and the texts are built on the box by the run's tool, never deployed as data.

SOURCES, each public domain by its date or its dedication, checked under tools/migrate_bible.py's strict PD-only gate and named with that reason: the World English Bible with the deuterocanon (eBible.org, dedicated to the public domain, the same translation as data/bible_en.jsonl), and the Douay-Rheims (eBible.org engDRA, the 1899 printing of Challoner's 1749-52 revision). Where no World English Bible edition carries a book canon.py lists for the Catholic or Orthodox layer, Brenton's English Septuagint (eBible.org eng-Brenton, 1851) supplies it, under its own Septuagint numbering, said on every response. The run's tool fetches each upstream file over https, refuses it unless its sha256 equals the hash pinned in the repository, parses it in a fresh directory as untrusted data, and writes data/ files of the existing slim verse row with the translation, the licence reason, and the book's layer.

LAYERS: the 66 stay as they are, byte for byte: data/bible_en.jsonl and every bible_<lang>.jsonl are untouched and every reading of a 66-book reference is unchanged. The added books live in files of their own, read only on a request for a book outside the 66, and each response names the book's standing from canon.py: which traditions hold it as Scripture, under which decision, and that the 66 are held by all. Books with Greek additions inside a 66 book (Esther's additions, Daniel's Prayer of Azariah, Susanna, Bel and the Dragon) are reached by their own names and never change the 66-book chapter they belong beside. Every book canon.py lists for the Catholic and Orthodox layers has text in at least one layer, or the step's note names it as missing with the reason; the Ethiopian layer's books beyond those (Enoch, Jubilees, Meqabyan) are named as a later run.

READERS: read_passage, the MCP tool and the site's passage reader resolve a reference to an added book (by name or common abbreviation, such as 'Tobit 4:15', 'Sir 3:30', '1 Maccabees 2:1', 'Psalm 151:1', 'Prayer of Manasseh 1') to its text from the World English Bible layer by default and from the Douay-Rheims or Brenton layer on request, with the translation, the licence reason and the book's standing. A reference that names no known book still reads as it reads today. The canon tool's report for a book gains whether its text is kept and in which layers.

TESTS, each red at the base where it should move: Tobit 4:15, Sirach 3:30, Wisdom 3:1, 1 Maccabees 2:1, Baruch 3:9 and Psalm 151:1 resolve with their standing; the Douay-Rheims reading of Tobit 4:15 is served on request; Genesis 1:1, John 3:16 and Psalm 23:1 read exactly as at the base; a 66-book reference never returns an added book's text; each added book's verse count in each layer equals the count in its upstream file; a changed upstream byte fails the pinned hash and nothing is written. The tool's parse is tested on a small fixture in the repository, never on a network fetch.

MEMORY: the engine's resident memory at boot does not change, since the layers load only on first use; the live check reads the engine's RSS before and after one request for each layer and states the growth, which must stay under 60 MB.
UNCHANGED: the gate's assay, the floor and the moat hold; the full suite passes against the baseline; tools/vocab_gate.py holds where it applies; no file under data/ is committed.

LIVE: after deploy and the build on the box, the site and the MCP face read Tobit 4:15 and Psalm 151:1 with their standing, the Douay-Rheims on request, and John 3:16 as before; the engines' restart counts are read before and after by the lead in a note.
goal: The keeping holds the text of every book the Roman Catholic and Eastern Orthodox churches read as Scripture, each on its own layer beside the 66 and never merged into them. The owner, 2026-11-11, on making Catholic and Orthodox Christianity a strength: 'Run down the list. This needs to be a strength.' Measured at master 85c3dda: data/bible_en.jsonl (the World English Bible) and every other-language Bible hold the 66 books only, including the Clementine Vulgate (bible_la.jsonl) and the Russian Synodal (bible_ru.jsonl); src/concordance/canon.py already names each tradition's books beyond the 66 on layers of their own (Roman Catholic, Trent 1546; Eastern Orthodox, Jerusalem 1672; Ethiopian), reporting who holds what and never judging, but no text of those books is kept, so Tobit 4:15 or Sirach 3:30 resolves to nothing. The usual source, bible.helloao.org, lists even its 'King James Version + Apocrypha' at 66 books, so the texts come from its upstream, eBible.org, as verse-per-line files.

text: MEASURED by checker-99 on 2026-11-11: the five eBible.org vpl zips, fetched once into a scratch folder and parsed with python -I as untrusted data. Zip sha256 (first 8 and last 4 hex) and Last-Modified: eng-web ae3b6aca..944c 2026-11-10; eng-web-c 87f2d2d3..028b 2026-11-10; eng-webbe 6e4dd930..67f8 2026-11-10; engDRA 7e267290..a7f0 2026-10-30; eng-Brenton 2d14f3c6..7917 2026-11-06. Every zip member carries its build time. Book codes in vpl.txt are eBible's own, not USFM: SOL EZE JOE NAH MAR JOH PHI JAM 1JO 2JO 3JO for 66-book codes; PRM is the Prayer of Manasseh, PSX Psalm 151, 4ES 2 Esdras, ESG Greek Esther, DNG Greek Daniel. Verse lines beyond the 66. eng-web: TOB 244, JDT 339, ESG 205, WIS 436, SIR 1383 (24 with empty text), BAR 213 (chapter 6, 73 lines, is the Letter of Jeremiah), 1MA 924, 2MA 555, 1ES 448, PRM 15, PSX 7, 3MA 228, 4ES 944, 4MA 484, DNG 530 (3:24-90 Azariah and the Three, 13 Susanna 64, 14 Bel 42); Esther's additions are merged into ESG verses (ESG 1:1 is 2105 characters). eng-web-c: the Catholic books only, text identical to eng-web except ESG 2, 1MA 4, 2MA 1 and DNG 6 verses; none of 1ES PRM PSX 3MA 4ES 4MA. eng-webbe: the same 15 books as eng-web, British spelling, 10 to 20 percent of their verses differ. engDRA: TOB 298, JDT 345, WIS 439, SIR 1591, BAR 213, 1MA 929, 2MA 558; Esther's additions as EST 10:4-16:24 and Daniel's as DAN 3:24-90, 13 (65) and 14 (42), inside the 66-book codes; no 1ES PRM PSX 3MA 4MA. eng-Brenton: TOB 245, JDT 339, ESG 252, WIS 436, SIR 1368, BAR 140 (5 chapters), EPJ 73, SUS 64, BEL 42, 1MA 924, 2MA 555, 1ES 448, PRM 15, 3MA 228, 4MA 483, DNG 422, Psalm 151 as PSA 151 (7); 315 lettered verse ids such as TOB 4:7a (TOB 14, ESG 88, SIR 12, 4MA 3, DNG 2 among the added books); Brenton has no TOB 4:15. data/bible_en.jsonl (31098 rows) renders the divine name as 'the LORD' (0 rows with Yahweh) and matches eng-web-c on 27100 of 27163 compared verses; eng-web has Yahweh in 5798 verses. Memory with the base's Bible class (src/concordance/verifiers/scripture.py), by tracemalloc: retained 2.7 MB for eng-web's 15 non-66 books, 1.7 MB for the DRA's added books with EST and DAN, 2.0 MB for Brenton's non-66 books, peak 17 to 24 MB while loading; the 66 today retain 12.5 MB.

findings: LAYERS and SOURCES: five of canon.py's Catholic entries (src/concordance/canon.py:113-128) are not books in any WEB file, and two are not books in any source. eng-web merges Esther's additions into Greek-Esther verses (ESG 1:1 is 2105 characters, Addition A plus 1:1; 3:13, 5:1 and 8:13 likewise) and carries Azariah and the Three as DNG 3:24-90, Susanna as DNG 13, Bel as DNG 14 and the Letter of Jeremiah as BAR 6. Brenton has SUS, BEL and EPJ as books, but Esther's additions only as lettered verses (ESG 1:1a ...) and Azariah inside DNG 3. 'Reached by their own names' needs a cut the plan never defines: which source and range, what 'Susanna 1:1' or 'Prayer of Azariah 1:1' reads (WEB DNG 3:24 is the KJV's Azariah 1), whether a cut inside a verse is allowed (eBible's terms say a changed WEB text may not be called the World English Bible), and what 'verse count equals the count in its upstream file' means for a cut book. The escape 'or the step's note names it as missing' contradicts 'reached by their own names'. Answer: for each of the five, name the source, a whole-verse range with its citation and the reference form, or name it missing and drop it from LAYERS.

TESTS and READERS: the Douay-Rheims follows the Vulgate's text and numbering, and the plan states a layer's own numbering only for Brenton. In engDRA, TOB 4:15 is 'If any man hath done any work for thee, immediately pay him his hire'; WEB 4:15's 'what you yourself hate, do to no man' is DRA 4:16. SIR 3:30 is 'The congregation of the proud shall not be healed'; WEB 3:30's almsgiving verse is DRA 3:33. TOB has 298 verses against WEB's 244, SIR 1591 against 1383. 'The Douay-Rheims reading of Tobit 4:15 is served on request' passes on either verse, and remapping DRA to WEB numbering would be generating a versification. Answer: each layer reads in its source's own numbering with no cross-layer mapping, every DRA response says it is the Vulgate's numbering, and the test pins the DRA's own Tobit 4:15 text.

SOURCES: 'the existing slim verse row' cannot hold Brenton. eng-Brenton's vpl.txt has 315 lettered verse ids, among the added books TOB 14 (4:7a to 4:7l), ESG 88, SIR 12, 4MA 3 and DNG 2. Every kept row carries verse as an integer (data/bible_en.jsonl), and Bible.__init__ skips any row whose verse does not int() (src/concordance/verifiers/scripture.py:83-86). A parse with an integer verse pattern turns 'TOB 4:7h Do that to no man which thou hatest' into 4:7 with an 'h ' prefix on the text, and keeps only the last of the duplicates. Brenton has no Tobit 4:15 at all; its 4:8-18 are 4:7a-l. Answer: say how a lettered verse is keyed and cited (for example 'Tobit 4:7h'), test it on a fixture line copied from the file, and count lettered lines in the count check.

src/concordance/verifiers/scripture.py:203-207: an empty upstream verse reads as found, so a miss is reported as a hit. eng-web's Sirach has 24 lines with no text (1:5, 1:7, 1:21, 3:19, 10:21 and 19 more). On the base's Bible class, resolve('Sirach 1:5') returns status ok with text '', and passage('Sirach 1:4-6') shows an empty verse 5. Answer: the plan says an empty upstream line is not written, or reads not_found with the reason that the source has no text there; it says whether the count check counts those 24 lines; and a test pins 'Sirach 1:5'.

BASE and LIVE: no gated ship path runs the build on the box. tools/deploy.sh only snapshots, transfers, restarts and runs its four gates (lines 52-162). Run 2026-11-01-green-suite already recorded that deploy.sh never runs seeds and that the lead may touch the box only through it. So the build would be by hand, with no snapshot or revert of what it writes, and deploy.sh's on-box gate grades the engine before the layers exist. Two traps follow. A request between the restart and the build can cache an absent layer, as the base's bible() caches Bible([]) for a missing file (scripture.py:296-299), and the layer then stays empty until a restart. And a pin on the zip fails on any eBible rebuild, since every zip member carries its build time (all five were rebuilt between 2026-10-29 and 2026-11-10). Answer: name the gated path for the build (pin, write, re-run the gate, revert on failure, restart) and its order against the deploy; say whether an absent layer is cached; pin the vpl.txt member; and say what the lead does when the pin no longer matches.

MEMORY is not checkable as written. No public GET reports the engine's RSS after a request: /systems serves only the boot roll-call ('boot' in systems.report, src/concordance/systems.py:261), so a checker cannot read 'before and after one request', and 'at boot does not change' has no tolerance, though boot RSS moves from restart to restart. Two engines run the same code (nh-engine and nh-mcp), and a verify that runs in a cell reads data files by path, so each process can load its own copy. Measured with the base's Bible class: 2.7 MB retained for eng-web's 15 non-66 books, 1.7 MB for the DRA's, 2.0 MB for Brenton's, with a peak of 17 to 24 MB while loading. Answer: the lead reads each engine's RSS on the box in a note; a test that boot and a 66-book read open no layer file replaces 'at boot does not change'; the 60 MB bound is per process.

READERS names three readers, but read_passage is also the oracle that ask.find_ref (src/concordance/ask.py:797-807) and console._is_bare_scripture_ref (src/concordance/console.py:73-84) use to decide that prose is Scripture, and classify (ask.py:1345) routes 'scripture' before verify, compute, decision and comfort. Measured on the base's Bible class with the added books reachable through passage(): 'wisdom 2', 'sir 2', 'bar 3', 'tob 1' and 'bel 1' go from not_found to ok, through its three-letter prefix tier. So 'yes sir 2 more questions' or 'at the bar 3 nights ago' would be answered with Sirach or Baruch. Crisis is checked first and is unaffected. Answer: say whether ask and the console reach the added books, and by which forms (for example full names and canon.py's aliases only, with no prefix inference), and add base tests that such prose routes as it does today.

LAYERS says every 66-book reading is unchanged, but the tests name three full names (Genesis 1:1, John 3:16, Psalm 23:1) that no design breaks. The risk is in the alias and prefix tiers of Bible._pick_book (src/concordance/verifiers/scripture.py:117-149). Measured with Ecclesiasticus, Judith and Esther (Greek) in the 66's index: 'Ecc 3:1', 'Eccles 3:1', 'Jud 5:1', 'Est 1:1' and 'Esth 1:1' go from ok to ambiguous. Answer: add these to the unchanged tests, or better, a test that every form of each 66-book name (the curated table, book_abbr, every prefix of three letters or more) reads as it did at the base.

TESTS: the count criterion cannot fail as planned. eBible's vpl.txt uses its own codes, not USFM: PSX for Psalm 151, PRM for the Prayer of Manasseh, 4ES, ESG, DNG and EPJ, and SOL EZE JOE NAH MAR JOH PHI JAM 1JO 2JO 3JO for 66-book codes. A fixture written from USFM codes (PS2, MAN, LJE, DAG) passes while the real file maps nothing. A count taken from the same parse agrees with itself when a code is dropped, and the clean clone has no upstream file to count. Answer: commit the expected line count per book beside the pinned hashes (this run's measure note has them); cut the fixture from lines of the real files; and have the tool refuse when a non-66 code in the file is neither mapped nor named as skipped (eng-web's 4ES, 2 Esdras, is not in canon.py).

done: BASE: master 85c3dda, in worktree concordance-2-canons on branch full-canons. The step opens only after run 2026-11-11-box-build ships, with master merged into this branch. One step, canons. It ships with sh tools/deploy.sh --build tools/build_canon_layers.py after green CI.

SOURCES, named exactly: eBible.org eng-web (the World English Bible, dedicated to the public domain, carrying every Catholic and Orthodox book canon.py lists for those layers) as the default layer, and eBible.org engDRA (the Douay-Rheims, the 1899 printing of Challoner's 1749-52 revision, public domain by date) on request. The strict PD-only gate gains a table keyed by source, not language, with each reason. The build pins the sha256 of each extracted verse-per-line text file, never the zip (whose members carry their build time); a changed text, an unreachable source or any other failure exits non-zero, so the path swaps nothing.

BOOKS AND NUMBERING: eBible's own book codes (such as PSX, PRM, ESG, DNG, 4ES, SOL, JOH) are mapped by a committed table; a code neither mapped nor listed as deliberately skipped refuses the build. The expected verse count of each added book in each layer is committed, taken from checker-99's measurement at line 3, and the build refuses any mismatch. Each layer keeps its own numbering and every response says whose numbering it is; lettered verses, where an edition has them, keep their labels and are never folded into a whole number. An empty verse reads as missing, never as found.

THE GREEK ADDITIONS are served as the editions hold them: Esther (Greek) and Daniel (Greek) as books of the layer; Susanna as Daniel (Greek) 13, Bel and the Dragon as 14, the Prayer of Azariah as 3:24-90 in the WEB layer's numbering, the Letter of Jeremiah as Baruch 6; a request for the Additions to Esther resolves to Esther (Greek) with a sentence that the additions are read within it. canon.py's entries say which of these each is.

READERS: the added books have a lookup of their own, consulted only after the 66's lookup fails, so every alias the 66 resolve today resolves exactly as at the base; Psalm 151 is reached by an explicit exception, since Psalms has no chapter 151 among the 66. Where text is read as a possible reference in prose (ask.find_ref, the console), an added book resolves only as a full reference with chapter and verse and a full name or a listed abbreviation that is not a common English word, so 'yes sir 2 more questions', 'wisdom 2' and 'bar 3' read as prose. read_passage, the MCP tool and /passage serve an added book's text with its edition, numbering and standing from canon.py; site/bible.html labels each reading with its edition, never WEB for every reading. The layers live in data/canon_layers/<edition>.jsonl, never bible_<letters>.jsonl, so /languages and /capabilities read as before.

TESTS, each red at the base where it should move: the WEB layer's Tobit 4:15 and the Douay-Rheims layer's Tobit 4:16 each hold the saying 'what you hate, do to no one' in their own words, and Douay-Rheims Tobit 4:15 is its own verse about wages; Sirach 3:30 (WEB) and Douay-Rheims Sirach 3:33 are the almsgiving verse; Psalm 151:1 and 1 Maccabees 2:1 resolve with their standing; Susanna 1 and the Letter of Jeremiah resolve as above; Sirach 1:5, empty in the WEB file, reads as missing. Every alias in the 66's lookup resolves exactly as at the base, named among them Ecc 3:1, Eccles 3:1, Jud 5:1, Est 1:1, Esth 1:1, Dan 3:24 and Ps 23:1; the prose cases above read as prose; a 66-book reference never returns an added book's text. The build refuses an unmapped code, a count mismatch and a changed text. Parsing is tested on fixtures committed in the repository, cut from the real files with eBible's own codes, never on a network fetch.

MEMORY, read by the lead on the box in a note: each engine's resident memory (nh-engine and nh-mcp) after the build's restart within 10 MB of the boot before it, and after one request to each layer, growth under 15 MB per engine; checker-99 measured 1.7 to 2.7 MB resident per layer.

UNCHANGED: the gate's assay, the floor and the moat hold; the full suite passes against the baseline; no file under data/ is committed; /languages, /capabilities and every 66-book reading are as before. LATER, named: Brenton's English and Greek Septuagint with the Psalms numbering map (the Septuagint run), and the Ethiopian layer's books.

LIVE: after the deploy and its build, the site and the MCP face read WEB Tobit 4:15 and Douay-Rheims Tobit 4:16 with their numbering and standing, Psalm 151:1, Susanna 1, John 3:16 and Ecc 3:1 as before; the engines' restart counts are read before and after by the lead.

text: MEASURED by checker-99 for plan two. Process memory, not heap: layer files written from the pinned-edition texts in the slim row with edition and licence fields (eng-web: 14 mapped books, 4ES and the 24 empty Sirach lines left out, 5987 rows, 2.4 MB; engDRA: TOB JDT WIS SIR BAR 1MA 2MA, 4373 rows, 1.7 MB), loaded in a fresh python process with the base's _load_verses and Bible: private memory grew 11.1 to 11.2 MB after eng-web and 11.3 to 11.4 MB after both, working set 10.2 to 11.9 MB, in three runs. This was on Windows, not the box's Linux. The 1.7 to 2.7 MB in line 3 is the retained Python heap, not RSS, so the 15 MB per-engine bound has about 3 MB of margin. No restart-to-restart spread of boot RSS was measured for the 10 MB boot bound.

findings: READERS and TESTS: 'consulted only after the 66's lookup fails' leaks added text under 66-book names. Measured with the base's Bible class (src/concordance/verifiers/scripture.py:117-149) as the added lookup, holding eng-web's books under the plan's names and consulted whenever the 66 do not answer ok: 'Daniel 13:1' returns Daniel (Greek) 13:1 (Susanna), 'Dan 14:1' returns Bel, 'Daniel 3:31' a verse of the Prayer of Azariah, and 'Esther 10:4' and 'Est 10:5' Addition F. Each of these reads not_found at the base, because the 66 have Daniel 1-12, Daniel 3:1-30 and Esther 10:1-3; the added lookup's prefix tier reads 'Daniel' and 'Esther' as Daniel (Greek) and Esther (Greek). 'Jud 1:1', ambiguous at the base (Judges or Jude), returns Judith 1:1. This breaks the plan's own 'a 66-book reference never returns an added book's text', and none of its named cases (Ecc 3:1, Eccles 3:1, Jud 5:1, Est 1:1, Esth 1:1, Dan 3:24, Ps 23:1) can catch it, since each resolves in the 66. Answer: say that the added lookup is consulted only when the 66 name no book at all (never on ambiguous, never on a chapter or verse a 66 book lacks); say that a 66 book's names never prefix-match an added book; and add Daniel 13:1, Daniel 3:31, Esther 10:4 and Jud 1:1 to the tests, each reading as at the base.

READERS: the prose guard is placed where it cannot hold. ask.find_ref returns the strict form 'word n:n' without validation (src/concordance/ask.py:778-780, _REF at 814), so 'yes sir 2:15 works for me' and 'meet me at the bar 3:15' are classified scripture at the base already (find_ref gives ' sir 2:15' and ' bar 3:15'). They answer with no verse only because the reader does not know the book. On the witness face, respond then reads the ref with resolve_ref or read_passage (ask.py:2078-2090), outside find_ref and the console, so a guard placed only in 'ask.find_ref, the console' lets those two read as Sirach 2:15 and Baruch 3:15. The plan's prose cases ('yes sir 2 more questions', 'wisdom 2', 'bar 3') have no chapter and verse, so they pass while this leaks. Answer: apply the guard wherever ask reads a ref found in prose, including ask.py:2082 and 2088, and add 'yes sir 2:15 works for me' and 'meet me at the bar 3:15' to the prose tests, each answered as at the base.

The strict PD-only gate gains a table keyed by source, not language, with each reason. The build tool, tools/build_canon_layers.py, imports only the standard library, writes its output as bytes with '\n' line ends, and is deterministic; it pins the sha256 of each extracted verse-per-line text file, never the zip (whose members carry their build time), and a changed text, an unreachable source or any other failure exits non-zero, so no build directory is added. Its listing entry in tools/box_builds.txt carries the output's sha256 (computed with the unit's own hash function), a memory cap, and its inputs: the book-code table, the committed verse counts and the pinned text hashes, which the path stages for it; src/concordance/build_pins.json carries the same hash.

BOOKS AND NUMBERING: eBible's own book codes (such as PSX, PRM, ESG, DNG, 4ES, SOL, JOH) are mapped by a committed table; a code neither mapped nor listed as deliberately skipped refuses the build. The expected verse count of each added book in each layer is committed, taken from checker-99's measurement at line 3, and the build refuses any mismatch. Each layer keeps its own numbering and every response says whose numbering it is; lettered verses, where an edition has them, keep their labels and are never folded into a whole number. An empty verse reads as missing, never as found.

THE GREEK ADDITIONS are served as the editions hold them: Esther (Greek) and Daniel (Greek) as books of the layer; Susanna as Daniel (Greek) 13, Bel and the Dragon as 14, the Prayer of Azariah as 3:24-90 in the WEB layer's numbering, the Letter of Jeremiah as Baruch 6; a request for the Additions to Esther resolves to Esther (Greek) with a sentence that the additions are read within it. canon.py's entries say which of these each is. A single-chapter addition is read in its own verse numbers mapped onto its span, and each response gives both: Susanna 1 is Daniel (Greek) 13:1, Bel and the Dragon 1 is 14:1, the Prayer of Azariah 1 is Daniel (Greek) 3:24; the name alone returns the whole span. The Douay-Rheims layer holds only the added books that have codes of their own in engDRA; its Esther and Daniel additions sit inside 66-book codes and are skipped and named, so a Douay-Rheims request for Susanna reads as a miss that says where that edition prints it.

text: For the builder and step checker, from checker-99's report on plan four (not findings): (1) MEMORY's 'after the build's restart' means the ordinary deploy's restart, since a build restarts nothing; the two boots before the deploy may be read from the boot roll-call lines of the last two restarts. (2) The live probes live in eval/live_probes.jsonl, so the ordinary deploy sends that file with the pin and the readers. (3) The output hash must not depend on line endings: the tool parses its inputs and never copies their bytes into its output. (4) The memory cap is set from a measured peak with margin, since on Linux the cap bounds address space and urllib with ssl maps far more than it holds. (5) eBible rebuilt eng-web's text on 2026-11-09; a change between the builder's run and the box build fails closed and re-pinning needs a new step. The step opens only after run 2026-11-11-box-build ships.
